issuing_body: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
title: Corporate Integrity Agreement Between HHS-OIG and NUWAY
jurisdiction: Federal health care programs / Minnesota Medicaid provider
supports: NUWAY entered a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement with HHS-OIG contemporaneously with its federal settlement.
The CIA covers NUWAY Alliance and specified NUWAY counseling entities and requires compliance with Medicare, Medicaid, and other Federal health-care program requirements.

Within 90 days NUWAY must establish or maintain formal compliance governance including a Compliance Officer, Compliance Committee, Board oversight, management certifications, written standards, training, risk assessment, and a disclosure program.
NUWAY must engage an Independent Review Organization within 90 days to perform reviews required by the CIA.
The Claims Review population consists of Medicaid Paid Claims for the relevant 12-month reporting period, subject to OIG discretion to select subsets.
For each Claims Review the IRO must draw a random sample of 100 Paid Claims and evaluate medical necessity, documentation, coding, submission, and reimbursement under Medicaid requirements.
A sampled claim without supporting documentation is treated as an error and its full reimbursement as an Overpayment for the CIA claims-review methodology.

The IRO must estimate the actual Overpayment in the population using a point estimate and two-sided 90 percent confidence interval; NUWAY must repay the lower limit of that confidence interval within 60 days after receiving the Claims Review Report.
The CIA requires annual reporting and permits HHS-OIG enforcement remedies, including stipulated penalties and potential exclusion procedures for material breach.
important_qualifications: A Corporate Integrity Agreement is a compliance obligation associated with a civil resolution; it is not itself a criminal conviction.
Claims-review error and overpayment determinations under the CIA are compliance/payment measures and should not automatically be labeled criminal fraud.
The CIA's five-year term is distinct from the $18.5M settlement amount; the agreement should be used to track compliance outcomes over time rather than treated as another monetary recovery.
